record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For a general input to the Steiner tree problem, is the minimizing Steiner tree unique?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2. Is a solution to the Steiner tree problem unique for a general input?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of points (called terminals). A Steiner tree for $A$ is a connected set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ containing $A$, and a minimizing Steiner tree is one that achieves the infimum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (total length) among all such connected sets. Equivalently, in the network setting, given a connected weighted graph $G = (V,E,w)$ and a subset $A \subseteq V$ of terminals, a minimizing Steiner tree is a subtree of $G$ that contains $A$ and minimizes the total edge weight.

Question: For a "general" (generic) input $A$, is the minimizing Steiner tree unique? More precisely, does there exist a notion of genericity (e.g., a residual or full-measure subset of the configuration space of finite terminal sets) such that for every input in this generic class, the minimizing Steiner tree is unique?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers (2025). A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of the generic uniqueness question for Steiner trees, and standard references treat uniqueness only in special cases (e.g., small numbers of terminals in the plane).

status_evidence.title: Steiner tree problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses NP-hardness and structural properties of Steiner trees but does not state a general uniqueness result for generic inputs.
status_evidence.claim: No general theorem on uniqueness of minimizing Steiner trees for generic inputs is stated in standard references.

status_evidence.title: Steiner Tree Problems (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on Steiner tree problems; uniqueness for generic configurations is not established as a general theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Survey literature does not record a resolution of the generic-uniqueness question.
